title: Effective Cartier divisors are nowhere dense
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme and let $D\subseteq X$ be the closed subscheme cut out by an effective Cartier ideal $\mathcal I_D\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal]. Then the open complement $U=X\setminus D$, with inclusion $j:U\to X$, is scheme-theoretically dense in $X$ [def-nagata-scheme-theoretically-dense-open], i.e. $\mathcal O_X\to j_*\mathcal O_U$ is injective. In particular its underlying topological space is dense, so $D$ contains no nonempty open subset of $X$.

source.place: Tag 07ZU (Divisors, Lemma effective Cartier complement is affine and scheme-theoretically dense)

proof.text: Choose for every point x an affine neighborhood U_x on which C is generated by a nonzerodivisor a_x, using [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal]. These neighborhoods cover Y. The support formula C.support intersect U_x = zeroLocus(C.ideal U_x) intersect U_x and the singleton zero-locus formula identify the image of the inverse image of U_x under j with the basic open D(a_x). This is compact since U_x is affine. The open embedding j reflects compactness of subsets to their images, so the inverse image of U_x is quasi-compact. The affine-target characterization gives quasi-compactness of j restricted over U_x, and [lem-pc-quasi-compact-local-on-target] gives quasi-compactness of j.

proof.text: Apply the already proved source-library theorem IsInvertible.isSchemeTheoreticallyDominant_compl_support, recorded in [lem-pc-invertible-ideal-complement-schematic-dominance], to C. It gives scheme-theoretic dominance of j directly, with no compactness assumption on Y. Together with the preceding quasi-compactness this is exactly [def-nagata-scheme-theoretically-dense-open].

source.place: Tag 07ZU, Lemma complement-effective-Cartier-divisor, density assertion and proof

proof.text: Mathlib gives dominance, hence dense range, for a quasi-compact scheme-theoretically dominant morphism. The range of the open inclusion j is precisely the complement of C.support, so this complement is dense. If a nonempty open V were contained in the support, density would give a point simultaneously in V and in the complement, a contradiction. Thus every open contained in the support is empty.
